$comment: Defects discovered in an implementation the corpus judges. A `documentExpressible` row names the case that reproduces it and that case stays in the corpus after the defect is fixed; every other row names the static check that detects it, because a process property is not carried by any document.

defects.title: The emitted document is not a semantic IR document
defects.evidence: `$onEmit` writes `{ schemaVersion, generator, types }`; `semantic-ir.schema.json` requires `contractVersion`, `source`, `package`, `types`, `occurrences`, and `extensions` and seals the object with `additionalProperties: false`.
defects.contractExpectation: Every conformance base validates against `semantic-ir.schema.json`; the prototype's output validates against nothing the contract publishes.
defects.staticCheck: Validate any prototype output against `semantic-ir.schema.json`; it fails at the document root.
defects.note: This is the root divergence: the prototype has never produced a document the published contract admits, so no case can be built from its shape.

defects.title: `schemaVersion: "1.0.0"` claims a contract version the document does not satisfy
defects.evidence: `const SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.0.0"` is emitted as `schemaVersion`, not `contractVersion`, and the document meets neither the 1.0.0 nor the 1.1.0 shape.
defects.contractExpectation: `contractVersion` discriminates 1.0.0 from 1.1.0 and the document must satisfy the version it claims.
defects.staticCheck: Compare the emitted key name and value with `semantic-ir.schema.json` `contractVersion`.

defects.title: Structural kind is the lowercased TypeSpec kind, not the closed IR vocabulary
defects.evidence: `kind: type.kind.toLowerCase()` yields `model`, `enum`, `scalar`; `navigateProgram` registers only models, enums, and scalars.
defects.contractExpectation: The closed structural vocabulary is scalar, record, enum, union, alias, sequence, map, and reference. A TypeSpec union is never walked, so a discriminated union — an explicit deliverable of issue #19 — is dropped without a diagnostic.
defects.staticCheck: Compare the emitted `kind` values with the `semantic-ir.schema.json` `kind` enumeration and with the set of TypeSpec declarations walked.

defects.title: Nullability is decided by a substring of a rendered type name
defects.contractExpectation: Nullability is a member a field carries, independent of presence. A type whose display name merely contains the substring is not nullable, and a rename can flip the answer.

defects.title: Recursion is decided by a substring of a rendered type name
defects.contractExpectation: Recursive references retain graph identity; recursion is a property of the type graph. A sibling type whose name contains the record's name is falsely recursive, and indirect recursion through two records is missed.

defects.title: Openness is decided by a substring of a rendered type name
defects.contractExpectation: Open and closed definitions declare whether unknowns are preserved, rejected, or surfaced. The prototype emits no `unknownPolicy` at all, so the unknown-field policy of every emitted type is undefined.

defects.title: Semantic role is guessed from the display name
defects.evidence: `semanticRole` branches on `name.endsWith("Event")`, `name.includes("Run"|"Evidence"|"Result")`, and `name.endsWith("Message")`, and emits one unnamespaced string.
defects.contractExpectation: Display names never substitute for stable semantic identity, and `roles` is an array of namespaced `<ns>:<name>` tokens orthogonal to structural kind.
defects.staticCheck: Compare the emitted `role` string with the `roles` array pattern in `semantic-ir.schema.json`.

defects.title: Identity is the dotted namespace path and moves with a rename
defects.contractExpectation: A semantic identity matches `^ix://…` and is stable under a display-name change; the prototype's identity is derived from the source namespace and the display name.

defects.title: A source locus is a `path:line` string with no column, no span, and no source identity
defects.evidence: `sourceOf` returns `${path}:${line}`; the absolute `location.file.path` is used whenever the file is outside `process.cwd()`.
defects.contractExpectation: `sourceLocus` requires `sourceIdentity`, `path`, `startLine`, and `startColumn`, and its `path` may not be absolute or traverse out of the source root. The `cwd` fallback also makes the output depend on the working directory, which the fingerprint excludes.
defects.staticCheck: Match every emitted `source` string against `common.schema.json#/$defs/sourceLocus`, and compile the same program from two working directories.

defects.title: Constraints are an object keyed by keyword and carry only `@pattern`
defects.evidence: `metadataOf` reads `getPattern` alone and emits `constraints: { pattern }` or `{}`.
defects.contractExpectation: A constraint retains its identity, keyword, operands, applicability, diagnostic code, and origin, in an array. `@minValue`, `@maxValue`, `@minLength`, `@maxLength`, `@format`, and `@secret` are dropped with no diagnostic, and declared loss lists every omitted identity while undeclared loss fails.
defects.staticCheck: Compare the emitted `constraints` shape with `semantic-ir.schema.json#/$defs/constraint` and list the TypeSpec decorators the emitter never reads.

defects.title: A discriminator is captured as a bare property name with no variants
defects.evidence: `discriminator: getDiscriminator(program, type)?.propertyName ?? null` with no `variants[]` and no `union` kind.
defects.contractExpectation: A discriminated union carries identified variants with payload types. Issue #19 names discriminators as an acceptance criterion.
defects.staticCheck: Compile a TypeSpec discriminated union through the prototype and observe that no variant reaches the output.

defects.title: Field type is a rendered display string, not a semantic identity
defects.contractExpectation: A field's `typeRef` is a semantic identity, and collection-ness is a `multiplicity`, not a suffix in a rendered name. Cross-package type equality becomes equality of rendered names.

defects.title: The emitter cannot fail
defects.evidence: `$onEmit` always calls `emitFile`; there is no diagnostic channel, no result state, and no failure path for a construct it drops.
defects.contractExpectation: Invalid, unsupported, or unavailable results emit zero files and at least one diagnostic, and never degrade to an empty model.
defects.staticCheck: Read `$onEmit` for any path that emits a diagnostic or suppresses the output file; there is none.

defects.title: Type ordering is locale-sensitive
defects.evidence: `types.sort((l, r) => l.id.localeCompare(r.id))` with no locale argument.
defects.contractExpectation: Locale is excluded from the fingerprint and identical inputs must yield byte-identical output; `localeCompare` without a fixed locale depends on the host ICU data and the environment.
defects.staticCheck: Run the emitter under `LC_ALL=tr_TR.UTF-8` and under `LC_ALL=C` and compare bytes.

defects.title: A duplicate identity is silently last-wins
defects.evidence: `types.set(item.id, item)` over a `Map` keyed by the dotted id.
defects.contractExpectation: Duplicate identities fail at exact source loci; they are never resolved by overwriting.
defects.note: The reproducing case exercises the contract rule the prototype violates; the prototype's own `Map` behaviour is a static property of its code.

defects.title: Everything outside one hard-coded namespace is dropped without a diagnostic
defects.contractExpectation: Declared loss lists every omitted identity; undeclared loss fails.
defects.staticCheck: Compile a program with a type outside the hard-coded namespace and observe that nothing records its omission.
